page: Amazon Web Services c8i.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, providing 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark results place the c8i.4xlarge in the top tier for Geekbench text processing and small-model LLM text generation, where it achieves 348.03 tokens per second. Single-threaded performance is strong, with Geekbench single-core scores and gzip compression rates falling in the top 25% of tested instances. Multi-core operations, such as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression, register in the average range. Memory bandwidth is measured at 121.51 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 70.53 GB/sec for large-block write operations, both aligning with average tier performance.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c8i.4xlarge offers a dense compute profile with DDR5 memory and advanced instruction sets, making it suitable for compute-heavy workloads without the overhead of local storage or GPU hardware. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps represent potential bottlenecks for I/O-intensive applications. The instance is suited for workloads such as text processing, software compilation, single-threaded data compression, and small-scale language model inference.
